claim: Theranos provided study data demonstrating that its system could be run accurately using only a finger stick as well as a traditional venous draw across large numbers of Theranos devices.

res.reason: Multiple trade and news outlets report that Theranos provided study data showing its system could be run accurately using a finger stick as well as a traditional venous draw, including a study of 818 subjects cited in coverage of the FDA clearance for its herpes test.

sources.title: Theranos Blood Testing Tech Gets a Boost from FDA Clearance
FDA Green Lights Theranos' Blood Test for Herpes

claim: Theranos' HSV-1 test costs $9.07 and is one of 153 tests Theranos makes available for less than $10.

res.reason: Multiple independent outlets, including Washington Post, Business Insider, Fierce Biotech and Medscape, report that Theranos' HSV-1 test costs $9.07 at the time of its FDA clearance in July 2015.

claim: The waiver means FDA determined the Theranos test and technology is reliable and accurate and can be used in a broader set of locations outside of a traditional CLIA certified laboratory, including Theranos Wellness Centers.

res.reason: The claim paraphrases a line that appears in trade-press coverage of the 2015 Theranos CLIA waiver (MathSP, citing FDA-related reporting), and the waiver itself is well documented: Business Insider, MedCity News, KFF Health News and BizJournals report that the FDA granted Theranos a CLIA waiver...

FDA OKs Theranos to conduct testing outside of CLIA labs

claim: Theranos' HSV-1 clinical studies demonstrated 100% agreement with the results provided by CDC.

res.reason: FDA clearance documentation for the Theranos HSV-1 IgG Assay (510(k) K143236) states the assay 'demonstrated 100% agreement with the results provided by the CDC' in the CDC panel testing, and Business Insider and Yahoo Finance report the company's release using this same wording.

claim: Theranos offers a comprehensive menu of lab tests in convenient locations in its Walgreens Wellness Centers in Arizona and California, with plans to expand throughout the country.

res.reason: The claim is presented in the present tense, but the evidence shows Walgreens terminated its partnership with Theranos in June 2016 and closed all 40 Theranos Wellness Centers in Arizona, with laboratory testing no longer offered through any Walgreens location.
